title: A geometric field stalk descends to a finite separable field stalk
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $\Omega$ an algebraic closure of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], $T$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and $\mathfrak p\subset T$ a maximal ideal. Then $F=T/\mathfrak p$ is a finite extension of $k$. There exists at least one prime $\mathfrak q\subset T\otimes_k\Omega$ with inverse image $\mathfrak p$, and every such prime is maximal and has residue field $\Omega$, with its structural $\Omega$-algebra structure. If for one such $\mathfrak q$ the local ring $(T\otimes_k\Omega)_{\mathfrak q}$ is $\Omega$ as an $\Omega$-algebra, then $T_{\mathfrak p}=F$ via the residue map and $F/k$ is finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Localizations are [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; tensor products of algebras use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tag 0384 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-upstairs), applied to a geometric field stalk, with Algebra Tag 030W (lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions), and the arbitrary-field descent paragraph of curves.tex Tag 0C4D. Finiteness at a maximal ideal is Zariski lemma, Algebra Tag 00FY (lemma-field-finite-type-over-domain).

proof.text: The quotient $F=T/\mathfrak p$ is a field because $\mathfrak p$ is maximal. Images of a finite set of algebra generators of $T$ generate $F$ as a $k$-algebra. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] to obtain $[F:k]<\infty$.

source.place: Tag 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz), field finite-type case; also Tag 00FY (lemma-field-finite-type-over-domain).

proof.text: Put $S=T\otimes_k\Omega$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat], $T\to S$, $t\mapsto t\otimes1$, is faithfully flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] to the prime $\mathfrak p$: it gives a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings), implication (1) => (2); field extension faithful flatness by Tags 00HP (lemma-ff) and 00HI (lemma-flat-base-change).

proof.text: Fix any prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$. It contains every $a\otimes\lambda$ with $a\in\mathfrak p$, since $a\otimes\lambda=(a\otimes1)(1\otimes\lambda)$. The bilinear map $(\bar t,\lambda)\mapsto(t\otimes\lambda)\bmod\mathfrak q$ is therefore well defined and induces a surjection $F\otimes_k\Omega\twoheadrightarrow S/\mathfrak q$. If $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ is a $k$-basis of $F$, the elements $e_i\otimes1$ span this tensor product over $\Omega$: expand each first factor of a pure tensor in that basis. Hence $S/\mathfrak q$ is finite dimensional over $\Omega$. It is a nonzero domain, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field] makes it a field. Thus $\mathfrak q$ is maximal.

source.place: Tag 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz), finiteness over an algebraically closed field; explicit finite spanning argument.

proof.text: Write $D=S/\mathfrak q$, now a finite-dimensional field extension of $\Omega$. For $x\in D$, linear dependence of $1,x,\ldots,x^{\dim_\Omega D}$ gives a nonzero polynomial $P\in\Omega[X]$ with $P(x)=0$. By [lem-weil-alg-closed-linear-factorization], $P=c\prod_i(X-a_i)$ with $c\ne0$. Evaluating in the field $D$ gives $0=c\prod_i(x-a_i)$, so some $x=a_i$ (the constant-polynomial case cannot vanish). Thus the structural map $\Omega\to D$ is surjective and, as a field homomorphism, injective. The residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ equals $D$ canonically: localizing the field $D$ at the images of $S\setminus\mathfrak q$ only inverts nonzero elements. This proves the asserted structural $\Omega$-algebra identification for every such prime.

source.place: Tag 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz), algebraically closed case; factorization and evaluation.

proof.text: Choose a prime in the hypothesis and put $A=T_{\mathfrak p}$, $B=S_{\mathfrak q}$. Since $t\notin\mathfrak p$ implies $t\otimes1\notin\mathfrak q$, the map $T\to B$ factors through a local map $f:A\to B$: a fraction with numerator in $\mathfrak p$ maps to the maximal ideal of $B$. The map $T\to S$ is flat by its faithful flatness in step 2. The localization $S\to B$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], hence $T\to B$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-comp]. Now [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] applied to $T\to A$ shows $f$ is flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] to $f$, and then [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] with zero ideal: $f$ is injective.

The hypothesis identifies $B$ with the field $\Omega$ as an $\Omega$-algebra, so its maximal ideal is zero. Locality of $f$ and its injectivity give $\mathfrak pA=0$. The residue homomorphism $A\to F$ sends $t/s$ to $\bar t/\bar s$ and is surjective (every $\bar t$ is the image of $t/1$); its kernel is $\mathfrak pA$, since $\bar s\ne0$. Consequently this residue map is an isomorphism $A\cong F$.

source.place: Tag 0C4D (lemma-nodal), arbitrary-field paragraph: descent of the field local ring.

proof.text: For every extension field $H/\Omega$, the $\Omega$-algebra identification $B\cong\Omega$ gives $B\otimes_\Omega H\cong H$, by $b\otimes h\mapsto b h$ and inverse $h\mapsto1\otimes h$. This ring is reduced because a field has no nonzero nilpotents. Apply [lem-trf-geometric-reducedness-local-base-change] with $R=T$, $L=\Omega$, and the chosen prime $\mathfrak q$. Its condition (2) has just been verified, so $A\otimes_kE$ is reduced for every extension field $E/k$. In particular $A\otimes_k\Omega$ is reduced. The residue isomorphism of step 6, tensored with the identity, identifies this ring with $F\otimes_k\Omega$.

source.place: Tag 0384 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-upstairs), using Tag 035W (lemma-geometrically-reduced-at-point); compare Curves Tag 0C4D.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-finite-extension-tensor-algebraic-closure-reduced-separable] to the finite extension $F/k$ of step 1 and the reduced tensor product of step 7. It yields separability in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. For a finite extension this gives separability algebraic as required: choose the finitely generated subextension $F$ itself in clause (2) (a finite $k$-basis generates $F$ as a field), and observe that its transcendence basis in clause (1) must be empty because $F/k$ is algebraic. Algebraicity follows from linear dependence of the powers of each element in the finite-dimensional $k$-space $F$. Thus the resulting separable algebraic extension over $k(\varnothing)=k$ is exactly $F/k$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Together with step 6 this proves the conditional conclusion.

lean.statement: theorem geometric_field_stalk_descent (k : Type u) (Ω : Type v) (T : Type w) [Field k] [Field Ω] [CommRing T] [Algebra k Ω] [IsAlgClosure k Ω] [Algebra k T] [Algebra.FiniteType k T] (p : Ideal T) [p.IsMaximal] : Module.Finite k (T ⧸ p) ∧ (∃ q : PrimeSpectrum (T ⊗[k] Ω), q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap T (T ⊗[k] Ω)) = p) ∧ (∀ q : PrimeSpectrum (T ⊗[k] Ω), q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap T (T ⊗[k] Ω)) = p → q.asIdeal.IsMaximal ∧ Function.Bijective ((algebraMap (T ⊗[k] Ω) q.asIdeal.ResidueField).comp (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : Ω →ₐ[k] T ⊗[k] Ω).toRingHom)) ∧ ((∃ q : PrimeSpectrum (T ⊗[k] Ω), q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap T (T ⊗[k] Ω)) = p ∧ Function.Bijective ((algebraMap (T ⊗[k] Ω) (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal)).comp (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : Ω →ₐ[k] T ⊗[k] Ω).toRingHom)) → Function.Bijective ((IsLocalization.AtPrime.equivQuotMaximalIdeal p (Localization.AtPrime p)).symm.toRingHom.comp (IsLocalRing.residue (Localization.AtPrime p))) ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable k (T ⧸ p))
lean.note: The structural Ω-algebra identifications are bijectivity of the canonical maps from Ω through the right tensor factor. The conditional conclusion is bijectivity of the canonical residue map to T/p, not an arbitrary ring isomorphism.
